## Headline

**Headcount grew to 412 (+8.4% from 380) while voluntary attrition fell to 8.2% TTM**, the lowest in six quarters. Engagement lifted to 7.8/10, eNPS to 38. Both moved with manager-effectiveness as the primary driver. We are hiring faster (38 days vs 42) without sacrificing offer-accept quality.

## What moved

Net headcount added 32 people in Q3. 38 hires against 6 voluntary departures. The **0-1y tenure cohort dominated departures** (18 of 34 voluntary leavers TTM), which is the standard pattern but worth watching when it grows. The 5+ year cohort lost only 1 person, a strong stability signal in the long-tenure base.

**Engagement score lifted 0.2pts to 7.8**, with **manager effectiveness up 0.4pts** as the largest single contributor. Comp clarity dropped 0.2pts. The only declining driver. Which is the watchout in the next pulse. **eNPS at 38** (up from 35) places us in the top quartile for our industry segment.

## So what

The quarter passes the basic checks: growing the team, retaining the team, engaging the team. All moved the right way. The **manager-effectiveness lift is the most durable signal**: it is the leading indicator that everything else follows from. Recommend doubling down on the manager training program (it expanded from 12 → 24 managers in Q3). The 0.4pt move came from the first 12-manager cohort completing.

The **comp-clarity decline** is the one yellow flag. Likely root cause is the new equity refresh cycle that confused vesting expectations. The People Ops note from W36 already flagged this. Recommend a written comp-philosophy doc going out before Q4 perf reviews.

## Talking points

- **Voluntary attrition at 8.2% TTM** is well below the industry benchmark of 12-15%. Do not normalize toward the benchmark. Celebrate the gap
- **Manager-effectiveness +0.4pts** is the headline driver. First 12-manager cohort completing training did the work. Expand the program
- **0-1y tenure dominates departures (18 of 34)**. Standard pattern. Worth deeper analysis if it exceeds 60% of departures next quarter
- **Time-to-hire dropped 4 days (42→38)** without offer-accept rate dropping. New recruiting structure is paying off. Credit the talent team in the QBR
- **Support team attrition at 14.8% TTM** is the outlier. Flag for the People Team Q4 review. Engagement also lowest there (7.2). Single team, real signal
- **eNPS 38 is top-quartile**. 76 promoters, 24 passives, 12 detractors. Worth mentioning to candidates in late stage interviews

## Risks + caveats

The Support team's 14.8% attrition + 7.2 engagement is a **localized concern, not a company-wide one**. But Support has the highest customer-touch frequency, so attrition there hits CSAT downstream. The CX dashboard already shows CSAT improving, which means the impact is being absorbed by the existing team. Bordering on overwork. Recommend specific Support team retention focus in the Q4 People plan. Comp-clarity decline is recoverable but real. If not addressed, expect it to compound in the next pulse.
